page: Amazon Web Services m8i.large is an entry-tier general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Operating on x86_64 architecture, this instance configuration provides 2 vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core with 2 threads via hyperthreading. Core clock speeds reach up to 3.9 GHz, paired with an extensive cache hierarchy that includes a 480 MB L3 cache. Memory is provisioned with 8.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The instance includes no integrated local storage and features a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, with zero integrated GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate an asymmetry between single-threaded efficiency and parallel capacity. In single-core testing, the instance exhibits robust performance, posting a Geekbench single-core score of 2169.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 34.22 GB/sec. Furthermore, the Xeon 6975P-C chip incorporates advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8). Conversely, multi-threaded throughput is constrained by the two-thread total, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 2735.0, a multi-core stress-ng metric of 2158.78, and weak ratings in Clang software compilation and PassMark database operations.

Memory bandwidth measurements register 160.17 GB/sec for small cached reads, falling to 22.61 GB/sec for uncached large blocks and 17.99 GB/sec for large block writes. In application benchmarks, the instance delivers 3.83 million Redis SET operations per second and 5.25 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Small-model LLM text generation (135M parameters) reaches an average 97.98 tokens/sec, while prompt processing falls to the lower quartiles.

Given its hardware scale, AWS m8i.large delivers cost efficiency primarily for lightweight, instruction-dependent workloads rather than heavily parallel tasks. The server is well matched for microservices, lightweight web serving, single-threaded processing queues, dev-test environments, and low-volume background jobs.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i.large is a general-purpose Nitro-based instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 vCPUs from 1 physical core running at 3.9 GHz, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache and 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU acceleration, and operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network throughput. Performance testing shows top-tier single-threaded compute, supported by instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX, alongside strong single-core compression metrics. However, due to its single physical core and two threads, multi-threaded metrics such as Geekbench multi-core (2735.0) and parallel CPU stress tests rank in lower percentiles. The m8i.large is optimized for lightweight applications, single-threaded batch tasks, small web servers, and development environments requiring updated CPU capabilities without high parallel density.
